api_description: A multi-cloud API for Cloud Automation Services

source.statement: THIS CONTRACT IS DERIVED FROM REFERENCE DOCUMENTATION, NOT FROM A PUBLISHED SPECIFICATION. VCF Automation (the successor to vRealize Automation and Aria Automation) ships no specification in the vmware/vcf-api-specs repository, so there is no machine-readable artifact to pin. Every path, parameter, property, type, constraint and status code recorded below was read off the rendered VCF Automation xAPIs reference pages on developer.broadcom.com and transcribed by hand; each page URL, the operation it documents and the date it was fetched are recorded in docs/official_sources.json. Hand transcription of rendered HTML is weaker evidence than a pinned spec: the reference may render a property differently on different portal paths, and it is silent about behaviour a client still has to decide. Wherever the reference is silent this contract says so and records the choice made here under local_decisions, marked as a decision of this repository rather than documented behaviour.

server.note: The reference renders every path as https://{api_host}<path>. No basePath prefix is applied beyond the per-operation paths recorded below.

security.note: The reference lists bearerAuth as the security scheme for both operations. Its curl example renders the header as `-H 'Authorization: <value>'` without expanding the token form.

operations.reference_summary: Creates a new policy, updates an existing policy, or trigger a policy dry-run.
operations.retry_safety: The documented summary makes this operation an upsert: the same call creates a policy or updates an existing one. The request body carries the policy `id` (type string, format uuid) and the reference marks it optional, so the client - not the server - may choose it. A request that carries a client-chosen `id` therefore converges on one policy no matter how many times it is delivered, which is what makes this mutating call safe to retry. A request that omits `id` asks the server to mint one, and every redelivery of that request creates another policy.

wire_rules: Call only the two operations named above, at exactly the method and path recorded for them.
A property that has no value is absent from the request JSON. Never send it as "", null, {} or [].
Never send a property marked server_owned; those are reported by the server, not supplied by the client.

A query parameter that is not being requested is absent from the request URL. Neither operation in this contract sends a query parameter, so both are sent with an empty query string rather than with parameters set to their defaults.
A request that has a body carries Content-Type: application/json. A request that has no body carries no Content-Type.
Send no header the reference does not name for the operation; the reference curl example for upsertPolicy carries Authorization and Content-Type only, so no Accept header is sent.

local_decisions.subject: status-to-outcome mapping for upsertPolicy
local_decisions.documented: The reference lists 200 OK, 201 Created and 202 Accepted for this operation and says of each only that the 'Operation doesn't return any data structure'. It does not say which status accompanies a create and which a update.
local_decisions.decision: 201 is read as 'the policy did not exist and was created' and 200 as 'the policy existed and was updated', per ordinary HTTP semantics. The mock in internal/vcfamock is pinned to this reading.

local_decisions.subject: 202 Accepted
local_decisions.documented: 202 is listed as a valid response status. The operation index for this API documents no request, task or job resource under /policy/api, so the reference describes no handle a 202 could be polled with.
local_decisions.decision: 202 is treated as an outcome this client cannot resolve, and is surfaced as an error rather than guessed at or polled for.

local_decisions.subject: reading the stored policy back
local_decisions.documented: upsertPolicy returns no documented data structure at any status. getPolicy documents a full Policy response body.
local_decisions.decision: Because the upsert response carries nothing to read, the stored policy is obtained with getPolicy after the upsert settles. This is forced by the reference, not an extra step chosen for its own sake.

local_decisions.subject: retryable conditions
local_decisions.documented: The reference lists 400, 401 and 403 as the failure statuses for upsertPolicy. It documents no transport-level or gateway conditions, as rendered references generally do not.
local_decisions.decision: A transport failure (no status observed) and the statuses 429, 500, 502, 503 and 504 are treated as retryable. Every documented status other than 200 and 201 is treated as terminal.

local_decisions.subject: recovering from an unobserved outcome
local_decisions.documented: Nothing in the reference describes what a client should do when a request is sent but no status is observed.
local_decisions.decision: A transport failure leaves the outcome unknown: the write may or may not have landed. Before the request is sent again, getPolicy is called for the client-chosen id. If the policy is there the earlier delivery landed and no second upsert is sent; if it is a 404 the write did not land and the upsert is retried. A response with a status is never ambiguous, so a retryable status is retried directly without a reconciling read.

local_decisions.subject: idempotency header
local_decisions.documented: The reference documents no Idempotency-Key or equivalent request header for this operation.
local_decisions.decision: None is sent. Retry safety rests only on the client-chosen `id` property the reference does document.
